topic_tag: a marsh above a harbor town
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: One hydrologist has concluded that the marsh serves the lower river as a kind of ______.

worlds.passage: Above a harbor town, a river crosses six miles of reedy marsh, and below the marsh the lower river runs past the town's quays to the bay. In wet springs the river soaks into the marsh's deep peat, and gauges below the marsh rise only half as far as gauges above it. Through the dry summer the peat lets the water out again a little at a time. The lower river keeps flowing past the quays in months when the river above the marsh shrinks to a chain of pools. One hydrologist has concluded that the marsh serves the lower river as a kind of ______.
worlds.explanation: The marsh's peat takes in spring floodwater and releases it slowly through the summer, so the lower river runs low in floods and full in droughts: the marsh is "a kind of sponge." "Sieve" fails because the passage concerns how much water reaches the lower river and when, not anything removed from it. "Spillway" fails because the marsh holds the floodwater rather than carrying it off. "Seedbed" fails because nothing in the passage starts life in the marsh.

sieve.quote: lets the water out again a little at a time
sieve.why: what the marsh changes is the timing of the water, not its contents

spillway.quote: the river soaks into the marsh's deep peat
spillway.why: the floodwater is held in the marsh, not shunted away

seedbed.why: the marsh's contribution to the lower river is water in dry months, not young life

worlds.passage: Above a harbor town, a river crosses six miles of reedy marsh, and below the marsh the lower river runs past the town's quays to the bay. The marsh is shallow and gravel-floored, and gauges show the river leaving it as fast as it enters, wet months and dry. Water from the mill ditches upstream reaches the marsh brown with silt and sawdust, and the reeds slow it to a crawl. Samples taken below the marsh run clear past the quays, and the gravel among the reeds lies under a thickening crust of silt. One hydrologist has concluded that the marsh serves the lower river as a kind of ______.
worlds.explanation: The river passes through the marsh at undiminished speed while its silt and sawdust are left behind among the reeds; combining the gauges with the samples and the crust shows the marsh strains the water, so it is "a kind of sieve." "Sponge" fails because the marsh holds no water back. "Spillway" fails because all the water continues into the lower river rather than being carried off elsewhere. "Seedbed" fails because the marsh takes material out of the water rather than starting anything that grows.

sponge.quote: leaving it as fast as it enters
sponge.why: the marsh stores no water, so it is not absorbing and releasing it

spillway.quote: Samples taken below the marsh run clear past the quays
spillway.why: the same water continues into the lower river, cleaned, rather than being diverted

seedbed.why: what accumulates in the marsh is material strained from the water, not young life

worlds.passage: Above a harbor town, a river crosses six miles of reedy marsh, and below the marsh the lower river runs past the town's quays to the bay. The marsh floor is hard clay laced with tidal creeks that empty into the bay a mile from town. When the river rises past a certain height, only the water above that level pours over a low bank into the marsh, and the creeks are back to their usual level by morning. In floods the lower river past the quays stays at its ordinary height. One hydrologist has concluded that the marsh serves the lower river as a kind of ______.
worlds.explanation: Only the excess water above a set level leaves the river, runs across the hard clay and out to the bay by the creeks within a night, and the lower river is spared the flood; combining these shows the marsh carries off surplus water, so it is "a kind of spillway." "Sponge" fails because the clay floor takes nothing in and the creeks are back to normal by morning. "Sieve" fails because the marsh changes how much water reaches the lower river, not what is in it. "Seedbed" fails because nothing in the passage begins life in the marsh.

sponge.quote: The marsh floor is hard clay
sponge.why: a clay floor cannot soak water up to release later

sieve.quote: only the water above that level
sieve.why: the marsh takes off a volume of water, not material from the water

seedbed.quote: empty into the bay a mile from town
seedbed.why: the marsh's role is moving floodwater away, not starting life

worlds.passage: Above a harbor town, a river crosses six miles of reedy marsh, and below the marsh the lower river runs past the town's quays to the bay. Each spring herring that have come up from the bay lay their eggs in the marsh's warm, shallow pools, where reeds hide the young from larger fish. The young stay until autumn and then swim down into the lower river. In years when a dry spring leaves those pools empty, the autumn nets set past the quays come up almost bare of young herring. One hydrologist has concluded that the marsh serves the lower river as a kind of ______.
worlds.explanation: Herring hatch in the marsh pools and leave them for the lower river, and when the pools fail the lower river's young herring vanish; combining these shows the lower river's herring begin life in the marsh, so it is "a kind of seedbed." "Sponge" fails because the passage concerns where fish begin, not how water is stored. "Sieve" fails because the marsh releases the young into the river rather than straining anything out. "Spillway" fails because the marsh carries no excess water away.

sponge.quote: lay their eggs in the marsh's warm, shallow pools
sponge.why: the marsh matters here as the place the fish start, not as a store of water

sieve.quote: then swim down into the lower river
sieve.why: the young leave the marsh for the lower river; nothing is held back or strained out

spillway.quote: come up almost bare of young herring
spillway.why: the marsh's contribution to the lower river is fish, not a route for floodwater
